p: Reading is a busy place, so it pays to think about when you go. Weekends and school holidays are the most popular times for karting, so book well in advance if you've got a big group or a birthday party planned.

Keep an eye on the calendar for big events too. Reading Festival takes over the town every August bank holiday weekend, when the roads, trains and hotels get very busy. Football and rugby matches can also make things busier around the south of town.
If you can, a weekday session can be a more relaxed option, particularly during term time. Ask about off-peak availability when you book.

As for the driving itself, smooth is fast. Look ahead to the exit of each corner, brake in a straight line before you turn, and feed the power in gently. Try not to fight the kart; keep your grip relaxed and let it flow through the bends. Lap times are recorded, so you can see exactly where you're improving.
Whatever you choose, give yourself a decent buffer before your slot, because Reading's roads can clog up quickly at busy times.

Reading's train links are excellent, with the Elizabeth line and Great Western services making it easy to reach from London, Oxford and the West. Then you can make a day of it, with a riverside stroll along the Thames or a visit to the town's historic Abbey Quarter, before heading home.
